To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
AM1 protein plays a key role in regulating expression of a subset (about 1%) of meiosis related genes in PMCs.

ameiotic1 (am1) mutants are defective in meiotic entry (am1-489) or meiotic progression through early pro phase I (am1-praI), and that transcriptome analysis of anthers from these mutants at meiotic entry or L/Z stage provides insights into the genetic network controlling these processes in maize.
AM1 is required for the expression of a set of meiotic genes that are essential for meiotic entry (am1-489) and progression to the L/Z transition (am1-praI).
In summary, our research is concerned with
defining molecular and genetic networks that control the onset and progression of meiosis in plants.

the identification of molecular players that regulate meiotic entry and prophase I progression, which will be essential for future studies on the molecular mechanisms of meiotic recombination in maize.
the identification of genes and genetic networks that are critical for meiotic entry, and early prophase progression in maize.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the transcriptome changes in anthers of both am1 mutants, am1-49 and am1-praw, are consistent with their cytological defects, and that AM1 is required for meiotic progression through the L/Z transition.
the am1-489 mutant is a meiotic arrest mutant, and am1-pral is a meiotic initiation mutant.
AM1 is a key modulator of gene expression during meiotic entry and prophase I in maize.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the transcriptome alterations in am1-1 and am1-prai anthers are consistent with the cytological phenotypes of these mutants, but also provide a glimpse into the meiotic program of maize.
am1 mutants are not meiotic defective per se, but rather meiosis defective because the meiotic entry and/or progression is not properly modulated.
AM1 is a transcriptional modulator of meiosis in the PMC, and a repressor of meiotic genes in the tapetum.
The main takeaway from our work is that
meiosis is a complex process, which requires precise regulation of the expression of many genes.
the transcriptome changes in am1-primarily affect meiotic cells, with only a small subset of misregulated genes affecting tapetal cells.

AM1 is not an essential regulator of the meiotic program, but a modulator of meiotic entry and prophase I progression, and the transcriptome changes associated with the am1 mutations reflect a more general meiotic defect.
